name: Pilate
overview: Pilate was a male Roman official who served as the fifth governor of Judea under Emperor Tiberius. He is uniquely identified in Scripture as the governor of Judea, holding a significant administrative and judicial role in the region. His governance is noted in the Gospel of Matthew and the Gospel of Luke.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Pilate' appears as a proper name without a specified meaning. He is also referred to as 'Pilate the governor,' a title indicating his role as a garrison commander or military leader. Additionally, the name 'Pontius Pilate' is used, identifying him more fully, and he is titled 'Governor of Judea,' confirming his official position over the province.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Pilate beyond his official role as governor of Judea. There are no known familial connections or personal relationships mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Pilate's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his position as the Roman authority over Judea during a critical period in the life of Jesus Christ. As the fifth governor under Tiberius, he had the authority to oversee legal and political matters, including the trial and sentencing of Jesus. His role is pivotal in the fulfillment of the divine plan for redemption, as he presided over the events leading to the crucifixion.
